name: High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression (EnCodec)
problem: Neural codecs either matched speech-codec bitrates poorly or needed one model per bitrate, and training was slow and unstable.
mechanism: Streaming encoder-decoder with a quantised latent space, trained end-to-end with a SINGLE multiscale-spectrogram adversary (cheaper and more stable than a stack of discriminators) plus a novel LOSS BALANCER in which each loss weight is expressed as the fraction of overall gradient it should own. Adds lightweight Transformer layers on top of the latent to squeeze a further 40%.
speedup_reported: Superior to baseline codecs across all evaluated settings at both 24 kHz mono and 48 kHz stereo; lightweight Transformers compress the learned representation by up to a further 40% while staying faster than real time. Baselines are named (Opus, EVS) but no GPU is specified for the real-time claim.
notes:
arXiv v1 is explicitly marked 'Preprint' and crossref/openalex find no peer-reviewed venue - it should be cited as a technical report, not an ICASSP paper. This is the codec behind VALL-E and therefore the audio-token-rate reference point for generative speech work. Compared with SoundStream the architectural idea is similar (RVQ + streaming); EnCodec's differentiators are the single multi-scale adversary and the loss balancer, which are training-cost innovations rather than inference-cost ones - worth knowing, because the inference cost of the two is broadly comparable.
